transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Yeah… I guess the biggest thing that made me come in is that my eating just kind of went completely off the rails. I’m usually pretty structured about food, like I track things and keep some kind of routine, especially because with work I need that structure, but I just stopped caring. Like, totally stopped.

I wasn’t really eating real meals for days at a time. It was more like coffee, protein bars, whatever was easy, and then I’d tell myself I’d eat properly later, but later didn’t really happen. And it wasn’t even that I made some intentional decision to diet or anything—I just wasn’t paying attention to it anymore. Then I noticed my clothes were fitting weird, kind of hanging loose, and that was honestly one of the things that made me go, okay, something is not right here. I didn’t even notice the weight coming off until it was already obvious.
Have you been feeling depressed lately?

Yeah. I mean… yes, I think so. It kind of hit me after this thing at work where the sponsor questioned my judgment. I know that probably sounds like a normal work stress thing, but it didn’t feel normal. It was like the bottom just dropped out from under me.

I went home and I just sat in my apartment feeling… hollow, I guess. And ashamed. Like I’d been exposed as someone who didn’t know what he was doing, even though normally I would’ve been able to deal with an email like that, respond professionally, clarify things, whatever. That’s literally part of my job. But I was sitting there staring at messages I should’ve handled and crying over them, which is not how I usually am. It felt embarrassing even being alone.
Did these feelings start after that work incident?

Yeah, that’s when it really seemed to start—at least, that’s the point where I noticed it clearly. After the sponsor questioned my judgment, it wasn’t just like I was annoyed or stressed for a few hours. It felt like everything just dropped out from under me.

I went back to my apartment and I remember just sitting there, kind of frozen, feeling this awful hollow feeling and just… ashamed. Like I had been exposed, like everyone was going to realize I wasn’t competent. And the stupid part is, it was emails. Normal work emails. Things I usually handle all the time without falling apart. But I was staring at them and crying, and I couldn’t make myself respond the way I normally would. So yes, it really did feel like it started after that incident.
Before this work incident, have you ever had another period like this where you felt depressed for days at a time?

I mean… before that specific work incident, I don’t know that I’d describe it the same way. That moment with the sponsor questioning my judgment is really the point where it became unmistakable to me. It wasn’t just being upset or embarrassed in the normal sense—it was like the bottom dropped out.

I went home and just sat in my apartment feeling completely hollow and ashamed, like I’d been exposed somehow. And I was crying over emails I normally would’ve handled without even thinking twice. That’s why it stands out so much. Before that, I can’t really point to another period that felt like that for days in the same clear way.
Have these depressed feelings been present most days for at least two weeks?

Yes. Definitely longer than two weeks. It’s been… I think about three months now since that project situation, since everything kind of fell apart in my head after that crisis.

It hasn’t just been one bad week where I felt embarrassed and then bounced back. Most days since then, I’ve had this hollow feeling, like I’m dragging myself through the day, and the shame from it just kind of stuck to everything. Even when nothing new is happening, I’ll wake up and it’s still there, that heavy, uninterested feeling. I keep thinking I should be past it by now, because it was a work thing and people have work conflicts all the time, but it’s been going on for months. So yes—most days, and for way more than two weeks.
Have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

Yeah… I have. I don’t really like saying that out loud, but yes.

It started more as this thought that everyone at work would honestly be better off if I just didn’t wake up. Like not even in a dramatic way at first—more like this heavy, matter-of-fact feeling, like I had become a problem people had to manage, and if I just wasn’t there, it would be easier for everyone. I kept thinking about it when I’d wake up in the morning, like, “Why am I still here making everything worse?”

And then after that meeting, I got really overwhelmed and I actually said out loud that I should just walk into traffic and be done with it. I heard myself say it and part of me was shocked, but another part of me felt like… I don’t know, like I meant it in that moment. It scares me to admit that.
Before this started three months ago, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?

I don’t think so… not like this. I’ve had rough patches before, sure, where I was stressed or down for a few days, but I can’t really point to another time before three months ago where it felt this deep and stayed with me in the same way.

This really started after the sponsor questioned my judgment. That’s the moment I keep coming back to, because it was like the bottom just dropped out. I went home and sat in my apartment feeling completely hollow and ashamed, like I’d been exposed or ruined somehow. And I was crying over emails—normal work emails—that I usually would’ve handled without even thinking much about them.

So before that, no, I don’t remember another two-week stretch that was depressed like this. This feels different.
Has this been making it hard for you to do your job?

Yes. It’s been… honestly, it’s been one of the worst parts, because my job used to be the thing I could rely on myself to do well. Like, I could be tired or stressed, but I could still keep track of the moving pieces. And lately it just basically fell apart.

I started missing handoffs that I normally would never miss. People would be waiting on me, or I’d think I had communicated something and then realize I hadn’t, or I’d send things late and then try to overexplain it and make it worse. I sent out strategy documents that, looking back, didn’t even make sense. Like I thought I was being clear, but people kept asking what I meant, and I’d reread them and feel this horrible sinking feeling because I couldn’t even follow my own logic in them.

And then it got to the point where my manager and corporate security took me to the emergency department. That’s humiliating to say, but that’s how bad it got at work. It wasn’t just me having a bad mood privately and still functioning. It was visible. It affected other people. It affected the project.

And at home it wasn’t much better. I stopped keeping up with normal meals, stopped doing hobbies, stopped doing basic routines. Everything became either too much effort or pointless. So yes, it has made it very hard to do my job. I don’t feel like I’ve been functioning like myself at all.
Do these feelings seem much stronger than what that work incident would normally cause for you?

Yes. Definitely. I mean, that meeting was bad, and I would’ve been upset by it normally—anyone would be, I think, if a sponsor questioned their judgment like that. But this was… it was so much bigger than just being embarrassed or frustrated at work.

It felt like the bottom just dropped out from under me. I went home and just sat in my apartment feeling completely hollow, like there was nothing in me, and ashamed in this really intense way. Not just “I made a mistake” ashamed, but like I was somehow exposed as incompetent or useless. I couldn’t shake it.

And then I was crying over emails—regular emails, things I normally would’ve dealt with automatically. I’d open one and just stare at it, and it would feel overwhelming and awful, like it proved everything was falling apart. So yes, it was much stronger than what that kind of work incident would normally do to me. It didn’t feel proportional.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I have. A lot, actually.

That’s been one of the weirder parts, because the things I usually do to feel like myself just don’t pull me in at all right now. I haven’t wanted to go hiking, which is strange because normally getting outside and walking somewhere with a view kind of resets me. Even if I’m stressed, I’ll usually at least want that. But lately the idea of planning it, driving there, putting on boots—everything about it just feels like too much, or like it wouldn’t matter anyway.

And photography too. I usually like editing photos after hikes or just messing with old shots, organizing them, adjusting light and color—that kind of thing can keep me absorbed for hours. But I haven’t wanted to open the software. I’ll see the files sitting there and just feel nothing, or almost irritated by the idea of having to care about them.

Even little routines, like logging meals, which I know sounds boring, but it was something that made me feel organized and grounded… I just stopped wanting to do it. And there’s this woodworking project in my garage that I was excited about before, and I haven’t even wanted to touch it. It’s just sitting there. Normally that would bother me in a motivating way, like I’d want to finish it, but now I kind of look at it and feel blank.

So yes, I’ve lost interest. It’s not just that I’m busy or taking a break. It’s like the usual things that keep me steady don’t really reach me right now.
